This study examines the underlying principles of object categorization within recurrent neural networks (RNNs), utilizing a visual model trained on ImageNet that achieves near-perfect accuracy. By integrating insights from neuroscience, characterization methods from deep learning, and auxiliary experiments, we demonstrate three key findings. Firstly, we identify a set of hidden units, akin to "tuning units," whose individual responses collectively encode categorization, even though no single unit does so alone. Second, we show that the model generates distinct, stable categorical representations, which are significantly more efficient in terms of sparsity compared to the highly dynamic and less sparse activity patterns observed during training. Secondly, we investigate auxiliary variables, revealing their function as mechanisms for error compensation; these elements maintain utility post-training but hinder categorical stability and increase circuitry sparsity requirements when manipulated or removed. Collectively, our work offers significant illumination into both the operational mechanisms of state-of-the-art neural classifiers and the potential functional principles governing cortical object recognition areas.

Non-Hermitian systems defined by non-reciprocity exhibit a skin effect, characterized by exponential edge localization. While much of the literature concentrates on first-order effects in Hermitian systems or those in 1D non-Hermitian chains caused primarily by non-reciprocity, this study investigates an extended 2D Hatano-Nelson chain featuring both non-reciprocity and correlations. Our findings reveal a modification of the skin effect induced by correlations, yielding a more complex redistribution of the localized frontier compared to the non-correlated 1D case. Additionally, we demonstrate a subset of eigenstates that defy both bulk polarization and the standard skin effect, a conclusion supported by visualization of eigenstates and analysis of eigenvalue bifurcations within the exception point.

This paper addresses the generation of quaternary Golay complementary array pairs (CAPs) through a novel construction technique. We establish that a quaternary CAP with dimension $L=N^2$ exists only when $N$ is even, thereby confirming a longstanding conjecture regarding this parameter constraint previously announced. Following the presentation of a general structure for achieving the optimal $L=N^2$ codeword length, specific families of these sequences are detailed, including instances derived from integers up to 20. Additionally, we introduce a distinct methodology that yields quaternary Golay CAPs with length $L \approx \frac{3}{2}N^2$.

This study examines Higgs boson anomalous vector boson couplings utilizing the CMS dataset from proton-proton collisions at the LHC, which totals 137 fb$^{-1}$ at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. Analysis proceeds within a Higgs effective field framework, specifically targeting the operators associated with $\gamma\gamma$, $\ZZ$, and $\ggg$ final states. Constraints derived for the effective field parameters Alphag, AlphazZ, and Alphag are consistent with Standard Model predictions. However, these limits are notably looser for the gluon-fusion channel compared to gamma and Z boson processes, a disparity attributed to the lower statistical significance of the observed excesses in those specific channels. Furthermore, this research investigates anomalous top quark-Higgs interactions within a dimension-5 effective field scenario involving the $\ttZH$ channel. In this framework, limits for the effective parameters lambda_t and lambda_t exhibit agreement with Standard Model predictions.

Unsupured change detection is a highly sought-after task in computer vision, yet it remains challenging because of the high variability inherent in before-and-after imagery. Although supervised methods are state-of-the-art, they depend on labor-intensive annotated training data, which is often unavailable in resource-constrained settings. In contrast, our work presents an advanced instance-based unsupervised change detection framework that requires no labeled data. By training an image translation model to align one image with another using only unsynchronized temporal pairs, we can identify changes as outliers on a feature manifold using semi-supervised contrastive learning techniques. This linearization approach allows for efficient access to all pixels, enabling significant improvements to current unsupervised techniques through the use of simple image pairs rather than complex temporal sequences. Experiments conducted on three public datasets demonstrate that our method surpasses existing unsupervised benchmarks and rivals supervised state-of-the-art performance on the ChangeNet dataset. Specifically, we improve the previous estimate by a logarithmic factor. Furthermore, our approach yields a formula that captures the precise asymptotic behavior of these representations.

The spin dynamics of three electrons localized on adjacent atoms in the silicon crystal lattice are governed by the Heisenberg spin exchange interaction (J), defined by the Hamiltonian H = J{P(1/2 - S_1 · S_2) - Q}. Here, P and Q represent projection operators for parallel and anti-parallel bond alignments of the three spins, respectively, and {S_i} denotes the spin-1/2 operator for each particle. We have performed an extensive first-principles study to calculate how varying the configuration of these three dopants influences J. Our findings indicate that the exchange interaction can be enhanced by up to a factor of two and increased by up to a factor of two through strategic placement of the three dopants in specific silicon lattice sites. This paper introduces LibOPT, an open-source software framework written in Rust that offers a comprehensive collection of benchmarking functions for optimizing algorithms in rust. Designed to be extensible, LibOPT currently implements 62 functions,  Wright-of which are sourced from Bäck's survey, 2 from Johnson et al.'s study, and finally 2 from Keppens et al.'s research.

This study investigates the local action of the Cremona group $\text{Cremona}_n$ on $k$-rational varieties $X$ defined over a field $k$. The analysis concentrates on the computation of the transitivity degree—the minimal number of rational points $Q$ required such that the group of $k$-rational automorphisms $\text{Aut}_k(X)$ acts transitively on them—and provides a comprehensive classification of varieties with a finite transitivity degree. The work begins by determining the transitivity degree for projective spaces and applies these findings to various known families of homogeneous spaces. Furthermore, the paper establishes a necessary condition ensuring the finiteness of the transitivity degree for $k$-forms of quadric manifolds and investigates the local structure of the unirational parameter space of bitorsors relative to the action of the stabilizer groups $\text{Aut}_k(X)$ at a single rational point.

This paper investigates the properties of the momentum distribution for $N$-particle quantum systems, denoted as $\psi$, within an $d$-dimensional space under periodic boundary conditions. The analysis contrasts two theoretical frameworks: an abelian setup featuring the $U(1)$ gauge group, where the total momentum is simply the vector sum of individual particle momenta, and a non-abelian structure involving $SU(2)$ gauge theory that includes a non-zero Higgs vacuum expectation value. In the non-abelian regime, a discrete set of non-zero boundary phase factors arises, dependent on the Higgs vacuum expectation value and breaking simple additivity. However, under specific discrete values for the Higgs vacuum expectation value, this complex behavior vanishes, reducing to a regime reminiscent of the abelian case.

We have developed a theoretical framework to examine how a charge-carrier density gradient within a semiconductor influences two-photon absorption (TPA) and photon pair entanglement. TPA occurs when a material absorbs a photon pair simultaneously, creating a single excited state. In our study, we assumed TPA probability depends on intensity and that photon detectors exhibit position sensitivity. By applying a master equation that accounts for TPA, photon diffusion, carrier drift, and decay, we analyze the dynamics of a TPA system coupled to an entangled photon source. Our numerical findings reveal that a carrier density gradient can separate TPA-induced electrons and holes spatially, causing the local photon correlation to shift from standard anti-correlation to full entanglement. Additionally, we demonstrate that a gradient enhances theentanglement fidelity of locally detected photon pairs compared to a uniform carrier distribution, achieving near-unity efficiency through optimized parameters such as the photon wavelength.

Consider the global squared uniqueness problem for the backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE)
$-Y_{t} d t + Y d M t + d Y t = f(t, Y, Y 0) d t + d Y t d W t,$
where $W$ serves as a standard Brownian motion, $M$ is a locally square integrable local martingale orthogonal to $W$, and both $M$ and its predictable projection $\langle M, M \rangle$ vanish in the Itô sense at the origin. We demonstrate that if the driver function $f$ fulfills a linear growth restriction with respect to both $Y$ and its historical path $Y 0$, then $|E| + E 0| \leq K (1 + E 0| 0)$ for some constant $K$, global squared uniqueness holds for BS $E $ t $. This result generalizes previous findings limited to sublinear growth conditions established by Hu and Peng, as well as those addressing global Lipschitz continuity found by Hu and Zhang. Furthermore, our finding establishes that within the framework of global squared uniqueness, the linear growth condition on $f$ is both necessary and sufficient.

Recent studies have demonstrated that adding regularization terms to robust control mechanisms enhances their resilience against sensor noise. Building on this, our paper introduces a robust reinforcement learning algorithm capable of automatically regularizing the policies it learns. We derive a robustness lower-bound for this framework and propose a constraint to maximize it as an additional requirement within the solution space. The strategy enforces a minimum level of likelihood noise in the dynamics model; paradoxically, this assumption of higher noise leads to more robust output actions. We validate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on a one-link robotic arm subjected to various stochastic noise conditions.

Coded caching is a well-established information retrieval method that minimizes network traffic by serving all user caches and server transmissions required for instantaneous network storage (ITNST) using network coding. Although prior research has achieved significant network coding reductions in coded caching, the fundamental limitations of coding efficiency within this context remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a framework that maps coded caching schemes to combinatorial structures known as set-systems, enabling an analysis of coding performance through properties of these set-systems. The authors establish the framework's validity by: (1) converting every coded caching scheme with a specific activation pattern into a corresponding set-system, (2) demonstrating that the resulting set-system attributes directly influence coding efficiency, and (3) uniquely retrieving a scheme from its associated set-system via a coded decoding scheme. Consequently, this approach offers a systematic, general, and unifying perspective on coded caching schemes and their coding efficiencies, while also suggesting new research avenues for enhancing coding performance.

The Scott model serves as a classic semantic framework for lambda calculus, characterized by its compactness and ability to define Scott domains via type theory. Traditionally, however, these domains were presented using classical logic and non-constructive principles such as the axiom of choice. In contrast, this paper introduces Scott domains within a predicative and constructive setting, thereby providing an alternative to the classical model. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this constructive formulation offers sufficient power for the predicative development of program verification and higher-order abstract syntax. This paper focuses on degenerate Eisenstein series defined on $ \mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Z}) $, which are associated with specific cosets of the Wil group. We establish a recurrence relation among these series that corresponds to the binomial expansion of a degenerate binomial theorem recently developed by the second and third authors. Furthermore, this relationship enables the series to be regulated using a process akin to Hodge theory.

Equipping mobile robots with arm-like appendages introduces additional constraints based on spatial geometry, which should theoretically aid in refining collision avoidance strategies by leveraging this specific structural information. Currently, most approaches model the robot as a collection of independent linear dimensions rather than utilizing its geometric structure. This work presents a new method that incorporates an arm's spatial structure to generate collision-free paths. The study defines two metrics: the Collision Avoidance Barrier Function (CBF) and the Collision Freedom Constraint (CFC). CBF operates within a reduced-dimensional space representing the relative distance between an obstacle and a specific point on the robot, while CFC functions in reduced space to denote the distance between any part of the robot and any part of the obstacle. While both functions can individually generate an avoidance trajectory, CFC often yields superior results when used as a component in the reduced-dimensional representation of CBF. The validity of this proposed technique was demonstrated through simulations involving robotic arms with three and four degrees of freedom navigating among obstacles of varying dimensions.

Natural language processing seeks to enable computers to handle the variety in how humans write and speak, a task complicated by factors including domain differences, stylistic differences, author identities, temporal shifts, and age. Synonym substitution is a core technique in this field, used to create new sentences from existing ones by swapping words with equivalents. While previous efforts have relied on extensive lexicon compilation or probabilistic topic models, this study introduces a method leveraging neural networks to map vocabulary into a shared semantic space. This allows the system to identify synonyms by measuring distances between terms and generates variations by navigating along semantic relationships. The authors test this approach on the task of single-word substitution and find results that match or exceed those of prior methods.

We introduce a method for implementing nonlinear Hadamad gates using optical imaging and frame dragging within a Bose-Einstein condensate, applying this tool to boost the efficiency of Ramsey interferometry by generating a highly nonclassical, number-split squeezed state through a stochastic two-stage optical process. Initially, the condensate is divided into two spatially separated populations of distinct number squeezed states via an entangling mechanism dependent on photon numbers. Subsequently, a stochastic imaging protocol induces correlated phase fluctuations between these populations. Consequently, our approach achieves a significantly enhanced sensitivity for stochastic Ramsey metrology compared to traditional protocols operating under similar resource constraints on classical states or those limited by standard Heisenberg-limited scaling limitations.

This paper investigates the intersection properties of non-degenerate, three-dimensional meromorphic maps into the complex projective five-space, $\mathbb{C}P^5$, with respect to a generic surface defined by the intersection of three independent planes. The study establishes that if such an map omets the seven possible combinations of these seven, it must degenerate. Furthermore, it provides an explicit exception list. The results generalize and improve upon earlier work by the authors and those of the Bloch.

This work introduces signature-based algorithms for computing Gröbner bases of systems of multivariate polynomial equations. These methods are particularly effective when a system is underdetermined, allowing the incorporation of heuristics to enhance computational efficiency. By combining these algorithms with a standard elimination strategy, we can synthesize robust signature-based algorithms designed to compute the complete solution set for multivariate polynomials. Experimental validation demonstrates the significant potential of these approaches.

This study investigates photon production in Cu+Cu collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 32 A GeV using the framework of perturbative QCD. By applying an effective participant area of 28 $\pi$b—derived from a comparison of Cu+Cu and PbPb collision data at the RHIC energy level of 200 GeV—the calculated rapidity density of photons at Cu+Cu collisions is approximately 1.4 times lower than that observed in Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV. This result aligns with expectations based on the number of participants, given that the Cu:Cu participant-to-photon production cross-section is roughly 70% of that for Au:Au under equivalent conditions. Furthermore, the analysis suggests a connection between the Cu+Cu rapidity density of photons and the charged particle density observed in Au+Au collisions at the same energy.

Let $H$ be a non-trivial $k$-uniform hypergraph. The function $\mathrm{ex}_k^2(n,H)$ denotes the maximum number of edges in a $k$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ vertices that avoids the configuration in $H$ twice. In this study, we examine $\mathrm{ex}_k^2(n,H)$ for $K_4^3$ by establishing several of its fundamental properties. We demonstrate that $\mathrm{ex}_k^2(n,K_4^3)$ is $\Theta(n^2)$, with the additional finding that any extremal $F$-free two hypergraph is essentially isomorphic to a complete bipartite $k$-partite structure. Furthermore, we analyze the monotonicity of $\mathrm{ex}_k^2(n,K_4^3)$ and show that it is monotonically increasing with respect to the number of edges in $F$. Finally, we consider $F$-freeness in directed settings, proving that $\mathrm{ex}_k^2(n,K_4^3)$ is $\Theta(n^2)$ and that the unique extremal directed graph is the transitive tournament.

This paper introduces an algorithm designed for real-time rendering of fan-shaped line joins in leafy trees using the OpenGL framework. While standard triangle-based approaches in OpenGL often result in visible artifacts within the join areas, this proposed method avoids such distortions by generating each join as an even-sampled set of points. It further employs depth peeling during the z-buffered rendering process to create anti-aliased, high-quality fan-shaped transitions between points. By anti

This study evaluates a quasi-interpolation formula utilizing the radial basis function (RBF) $\phi$ with a conditionally positive definite of order one, alongside its finite difference approximation $\nabla^2\phi$ to order zero, where $0 < l \leq 1$. It further demonstrates theoretically that this formula, along with its associated difference operator, preserves monotonicity within a sufficiently small neighborhood. Based on these properties, we derive a novel universal RBF quasi-interpolation formula incorporating the Qi-interpolation method and analyze how the chosen neighbor radius influences the resulting convexity. The theoretical claims regarding monotonicity and convexity preservation are substantiated numerically. Additionally, we compare the accuracy of this new RBF quasi-interpolation approach against both the multiple quadratic RBF and the multiple quadratic RBF combined with a difference term.

Pulsar winds interacting with the interstellar medium generate pulsar halos, emitting radiation across the TeV energy spectrum. Given their ubiquity, these halos could potentially resolve both the diffuse TeV gamma-ray and cosmic positron anomalies. We present a novel methodology to assess their explanatory power by constructing a halo model utilizing a sample of 100 pulsars identified via Parkes and Fermi observations. Leveraging advanced tools such as GalaxySim and GALPROP, we simulate halo emission profiles and calculate energy spectra. Our results indicate that while individual pulsars fail to account for the observed excesses, a combined emission from this specific group of 100 pulsars could explain the data. We suggest that a halo model incorporating these known pulsars serves as a vital component for future analyses of these anomalies.

Although Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in computer vision, their performance is often limited by the scarcity of labeled training data. To address this, researchers have turned to data augmentation strategies that enhance CNN efficacy by creating synthetic variants of existing images. This study presents a novel, simple, and computationally efficient masking technique—super pixel delimiting masks—as a form of augmentation. These masks preserve the semantic integrity of original scenes while introducing significant visual diversity, thereby serving as effective additional training examples. Experiments conducted on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 benchmarks demonstrate that this method consistently improves upon baseline classifiers, including those augmented through traditional techniques such as whitening and color jittering.

We examine citation patterns within climate change literature to determine whether it maintains a specialized niche or functions as part of broader scientific discourse. Our evidence, drawn from top-tier general interest science publications and leading economics journals, indicates that interest among these communities has grown over the last two decades. Furthermore, these publications cite specialized climate sources more frequently than one might expect based on mere topic relevance, suggesting an active engagement with the field rather than reliance solely on existing expertise. Our analysis also reveals that the frequency of citations to these specialized sources correlates with the degree of a given field's inherent relevance to the subject matter. Ultimately, our findings imply that policymakers track climate change developments with less intensity compared to the broader scientific community and professional economists, potentially driven by the fact that both general interest and economics sources often draw upon research conducted within specialized climate journals.

This paper introduces a data-driven control strategy tailored for soft robotic systems, leveraging the theoretical framework of the Koopman operator. The approach begins by constructing a discrete-time dynamical model of the sensor dynamics from historical data using a neural network, a process devoid of the need for mathematical forward models of forward dynamics. Subsequently, a control law is synthesized on this estimated koopman operator framework to optimize performance. Finally, the method's viability is demonstrated through a case study involving a deformable soft tower, confirming its practical application and effectiveness.

We introduce a new method for optimizing the parameters of the Wavefunction, designed to accelerate convergence toward minimal energy states by leveraging information about the current wavefunction. This approach, referred to as "Natural Gradient Descent," utilizes a metric tensor derived from overlaps between perturbed wavefunctions to guide more efficient gradient calculations within the parameter space. By accounting for the curvature inherent in this geometry, the natural gradient method achieves significantly faster convergence compared to standard optimization techniques like gradient descent. We demonstrate the superiority of natural gradient optimization through applications to both model systems and realistic many-body scenarios, including a two-dimensional optical lattice hosting a single band of fermions with short-range interactions under various Hamiltonians. Our numerical simulations reveal pronounced superconvergence effects in systems exhibiting strong correlations, particularly near Mott insulator phases, a phenomenon we attribute to the wavefunction's inherent structure. We further examine how wavefunction flexibility and wavefunction optimization influence these observed superconvergence effects.

The feature observed in the optical/near-IR spectra of high-redshift active galactic nuclei (AGNs) at wavelengths around 1 micron is widely accepted to be a superposition of a blue, Fe II-emitting component and a red, dust-continuum component. This study presents a high-resolution, high-redshift AGN sample with spectral fitting results that support the standard two-component model. We find that the spectral shape of the blue Fe II component is consistent with previous research, and the relative contributions of dust and dust-free Fe II emission vary among objects. Furthermore, the slope of the blue Fe II emission correlates with the AGN's Eddington ratio, indicating a stronger blue component in high Eddington-ratio sources. Additionally, we demonstrate that spectral decomposition offers a reliable method for estimating the Eddington ratio across diverse high-redshift AGN populations.

This research introduces Lite-ProSENet, a streamlined deep learning framework designed to predict overall survival in lung cancer by leveraging limited multi-modal CT features. The methodology employs attention mechanisms and feature selection techniques to identify the most informative areas of interest and reduce dimensionality, thereby preventing overfitting. The model is trained using sparse labels in the form of continuous survival times. To validate its efficacy, we conducted experiments on two datasets: the LUNMIA-Lung-Radiomics-Life-Expectancy dataset and a newly compiled LUNMIA-Life-Expectancy subset of the LUNMIA-Chest-Tomography dataset. The results demonstrate that Lite-ProSet achieves the highest performance to date for predicting survival time, significantly lowering computational complexity and limited data requirements compared to prior art. Specifically, on LUNMIA-RL, the model attained a C-index of 0.782 and a RMSE of 1.015 years; similarly, on the curated time-subset LUNMIA-CTE dataset, it reached a C-index of 0.780 and a RMSE of 1.016 years when evaluated with 5-year post-treatment label data.

Representing the internal states of an agent is crucial for understanding capabilities and progress within language-based learning systems, such as reinforcement learning. However, current learning approaches, including those that utilize human feedback, often result in internal state representations that are mathematically efficient for the model but consist of meaningless numbers rather than understandable concepts. This paper introduces a framework for learning linguistically interpretable internal states by defining a contrastive loss function that aligns dimension meanings with provided descriptive prompts through state sampling. We apply this interpretable state system to model first-order skills defined as pairs of (precondition, postcondition), a task for which state interpretations are straightforward to articulate. Additionally, this state space serves as an improved foundation for modeling hierarchical skills, where high-level state meanings are synthesized from lower-level interpretations. Experimental results across writing-to-learn tasks and simulation environments with varying degrees of complexity demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach both in creating meaningful state representations and leveraging them for enhanced model performance.

We introduce a novel deep learning framework for reconstructing non-Gaussianity in late-time nonlinearity using galaxy redshift surveys. The method processes a segment of simulated galaxy catalogs to produce the corresponding power spectrum, $\Delta P/k^2$, treating it as both an input and output ground truth for training. The model is then evaluated on an independent galaxy catalog segment. Results indicate that for a fixed redshift range, the reconstruction accuracy degrades as the wave number $k$ increases, though it remains sufficiently precise for use as bias terms in high-precision cosmological analyses at the scales relevant to current and future surveys. Additionally, we demonstrate that the method successfully reconstructs the signal even when the observed galaxy sample has smaller number densities than the training datasets, maintaining the highest fidelity within the $k < 0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ regime.

This paper investigates the irreducibility of certain tensor products concerning universal enveloping algebras. Specifically, let $G$ be a simple simply-connected Lie group with universal enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g)$, and let $\mathfrak h$ denote a maximal toral subalgebra such that $U(\mathfrak g)$-module $\mathfrak g$ acts freely on $U(\mathfrak g)$. The authors examine the conditions under which the tensor product of specific highest weight $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules and free $U(\mathfr g)$-modules remains irreducible. They further explore the question of how these tensor product isomorphisms relate to the underlying irreducibility properties. As an application, these findings are utilized to characterize the automorphism groups of free $U(\mathfr g)$-modules in terms of their weights.

Recent years have witnessed a surge in research dedicated to automatically determining the emotional sentiment conveyed by tweets. This study presents a classification framework utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to identify sentiment polarity in English tweets. The proposed method employs pre-trained word embeddings to represent words and feeds these into an LSTM model that is refined through back-propagation. The resulting framework is straightforward and effective, performing well on the publicly available Twitter Sentiment UIUC dataset.

Role-playing within a natural language dialogue system involves adopting a specific character and maintaining consistency throughout the interaction. However, prior studies indicate that systems often fail to sustain these assigned roles during organic conversations, resulting in measurable drops in performance. To address this issue, we introduce a conditional generation technique where the system's role definition serves as a conditional input for text production. This approach not only enhances role consistency but also improves overall dialogue performance, as demonstrated by a significant 10% increase in F1 score relative to baseline models.

Background radiation from gravitational waves offers valuable insights into gravitational wave sources and the universe's history. This study investigates a background generated by stochastic gravitational wave memory arising from population III stars. This signal originates from the nonlinear GW memory effect, which stems from the coupling between GWs and metric perturbations. We find that this stochastic memory background exhibits a flatter frequency dependence than non-memory signals generated by the same sources, with a slope of $f^{-2/3}$ compared to $f^{-7/3}$ in the non-memory regime. Additionally, this memory background dominates over the non-memory signal across all frequencies within the LIGO detection band.

Ongoing research into word suggestion has largely concentrated on algorithms driven solely by semantic or syntactic principles, frequently overlooking the complementary strengths offered by the opposite approach. To address this gap, we introduce a new word suggestion model that integrates both semantic and syntactic analysis. Extensive testing against two established datasets demonstrates that these hybrid architectures consistently outperform systems relying exclusively on a single methodology. Furthermore, our analysis identifies an optimal balance between syntactic and semantic features within the model, validating that combining both sources enhances word prediction accuracy.

Attention networks have proven highly effective in learning to rank items by predicting relevance for query-paired datasets. However, standard attention implementations often struggle to effectively capture attention within recommendation contexts due to fundamental differences in data characteristics. To address this, we introduce RecANet, a recommendation attention network designed to capture local and global user-item attention through a novel user-aware state transformation. This approach explicitly models user preferences to enhance the relevance of recommended items. Additionally, we propose a RecANet-driven graph attention network, GraphANet, to incorporate relational information from users and items for further ranking enhancement. Experimental results indicate that both RecANet and GraphANet significantly outperform leading baseline methods and existing state-of-the-art approaches across various evaluation metrics.

We demonstrate that certain random walks by active dimers can be modeled as Gaussian random walks featuring Gaussian-switched Gaussian velocities. In these simulations, the dimers function as rigid rods equipped with an asymmetric, Gaussian velocity profile along their surface, where this profile's sign is governed by the center-of-mass orientation. The mechanism operates similarly to a steering wheel found in giant vehicles: oriented surface movement acts as the wheel, directing the overall motion even when the magnitude of applied forces and local velocities varies.

The paper presents a new method for generating the conforming Delaunay tetrahedralization of polyhedral fractures within a porous medium, aiming to support efficient simulation. This is achieved by adapting and enhancing an existing technique for 2D intrusions; the improved version efficiently handles fractures of varying complexities by introducing multiple control points on their surfaces. The resulting meshe, where a quality Delaunay tetrahedralization conformingly intersects the fracture volume, is constructed without requiring any manual post-processing.

This paper addresses the Minimum Convex Cover Problem, where the objective is to identify the smallest radius R such that no more than K of n swarming drones can be covered within a disk of that size. The goal is to select K drones in a way that minimizes the resulting disk's area. The study establishes the problem's NP-hardness and introduces a polynomial-time approximation algorithm with a K-approximation guarantee. Furthermore, a modification of this approach is designed to minimize the maximum first-moment deviation (m₁) of the chosen subset, a metric reflecting the dispersion of the subset's centroid. This optimization enhances the efficiency of applications involving balanced load distribution, such as search and rescue missions. Finally, approximation bounds for several additional approximation schemes are derived.

We present a method for constructing graphs where the eigenvalue $-1$ appears exactly once in a single Seidel vector. Furthermore, we analyze seidel graphs derived from modifications of bipartite graphs and connected chain graphs to show the following: the Seidel matrix of a connected chain graph always exhibits $-1$ as an eigenvalue with multiplicity one, and adding a single edge to a bipartite matrix's complement results in a Seidel matrix that also exhibits $-1$ as a single eigenvalue.

This study addresses a non-standard optimal consumption problem within stochastic control, in which current control inputs influence the stochastic dynamic's evolution not only immediately but also at a future time point, creating a stochastic delayed feedback loop. This mechanism creates a complex, two-way information flow: a forward path from the present to its delayed self and a backward path linking a future state back to its own past. Our model incorporates delays that are not merely fixed but are also stochastic, potentially sharing randomness with the Brownian motion driving the system's noise. Under the assumption of logarithmic utility, which allows for explicit mathematical solutions, the paper provides both the theoretical derivation and numerical simulations of optimal consumption policies.

The eigenvalue problems associated with the Dirac operator map directly to Heun's equation and can be modeled using tridiagonal operators. This work presents novel tridiagonal operators that yield natural extensions of both Heun's equation and Clausen's equation, simultaneously addressing quadrilateral and its specific instance, the Dirac equation. Furthermore, we derive expansion coefficients for these solutions in terms of power series.

This paper investigates average effective communication performance in heterogeneous vehicular networks (HNs) equipped with relays. First, we derive a closed-form expression for the average effective rate (AER) of base station (BS)-connected users. Subsequently, we formulate the AER for relay-associated users and determine the optimal placement for relays to maximize this metric. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of relay deployments on users' AER and the corresponding rate loss. Our findings reveal that while relay networks generally offer users higher effective rates than direct BS connections, the magnitude of rate gain varies based on the network topology, user distribution, and the specific link being served. Additionally, we examine how the average effective rate (AER) degrades as user data rates increase. Surprisingly, simulations indicate that relay networks do not consistently outperform direct BS links for all users; rather, whether relays reduce rate loss depends entirely on user location and current channel conditions.

Wikipedia serves as a vast, open encyclopedia maintained by a community of volunteer editors whose actions can reveal an article's quality through textual analysis. Additionally, individual editing behaviors offer insights that complement human assessments, specifically by enabling the use of editorial reverts as proxies for quality judgments. This study investigates how to leverage both factors to enhance supervised learning models for classifying sentence quality labels. We analyze the relationship between editing behaviors and quality dimensions, assess label consistency across revision pairs, and examine correlation patterns among reversals to improve prediction robustness. Furthermore, we employ a co-training approach to utilize reversal data for strengthening the model. Our findings demonstrate that accounting for temporal consistency in reversals and applying co-training jointly improve the robustness and accuracy of our learning systems.

Knowledge distillation serves as a widely adopted method for enhancing an ensemble of classifiers by enabling a smaller model to learn from larger ones. While existing techniques primarily rely on soft target probabilities to transfer knowledge, they often lack sufficient information to effectively replace data for tasks like adversarial training. This paper introduces Decision-Based Black-Box Distillation (DB3), a new approach that demonstrates knowledge solely through the classification decisions of the teacher model. By providing clear example sets of positive and negative instances derived from teacher outputs, DB3 constructs an informative approximation of the teacher's data manifold. Crucially, this methodology requires access only to final classification decisions, making it ideal for scenarios where internal model structures are inaccessible. We demonstrate the versatility of DB3 in two key areas: first, it successfully facilitates knowledge transfer in settings with no model access (black-box), and second, it significantly enhances teacher resilience during adversarial training. When compared to standard black-box methods, DB3 improves distillation accuracy by 3.2% on average; furthermore, it yields adversarial training accuracy gains of 3.5% over current best practices.

This study reports the measurement of the $CP$-violating asymmetries for $B^0_s\to J/\psi\pi^+\pi^-$, $B^0_s\to K^+\pi^-$, and $B^0_s\to K^+K^-\pi^-$, alongside the determination of the corresponding branching fractions. Data were collected using the LHCb detector with an integrated luminosity of $3.0\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The reported branching fraction values are $\mathcal{B}(B^0_s\to J/\psi\pi^+\pi^-) = (1.46 \pm 0.20)\times 10^{-5}$, $\mathcal{B}(B^0_s\to K^+\pi^-\) = $(2.07 \pm 0.10)\times 10^{-5}$, and $\mathcal{B}(B^0_s\to K^+K^-\pi^-\) = $(1.76 \pm 0.10)\times 10^{-5}$, where the uncertainties are approximately $14\%$, $5\%$, and $6\%$, respectively. Additionally, the paper presents the first observation of the $CP$-violating asymmetry in the $B^0_s\to K^+\pi^-\) channel

We introduce a framework for classical T-duality based on non-geometric Ramond–ond–spinor fields, utilizing $C^*$-algebras. Within this setup, we associate a continuous-trace algebra to any principal bundle formed by a free action of a Lie group over a manifold and demonstrate corresponding properties for its T-duals. Consequently, we argue that non-geometric T-bundles featuring T-dual algebras possessing the "continous-trace" property serve as a reliable indicator of an underlying geometric structure within the non-geometric context.

Imitation learning typically depends on expert demonstrations to facilitate effective imitation, yet acquiring these demonstrations can be difficult or impossible in many practical scenarios. Although recent advances in behavior-clustering and skill-learned algorithms have reduced this limitation by only requiring a few examples per skill, they still face the challenge of determining skill clusters without prior knowledge. This study introduces Co-Imitation Learning, a novel co-reinforcement and co-imitation approach that eliminates the need for any such demonstration data. By enabling agents to collaborate through mutual reinforcement and imitation, the method jointly acquires shared world models and shared preference models. We validate Co-Imitation Learning across various tasks, including shared navigation, shared navigation with object manipulation, shared navigation with a multi-agent environment, and shared navigation with a multi-agent environment, demonstrating its efficacy in these complex settings.

The authors introduce a bias adjustment method for sequential decoding applied to binary-input symmetric discrete memoryless channels. In this approach, the polar cutoff rate serves as the bias value for exploring the tree structure. They demonstrate theoretically and through simulations that utilizing this choice keeps the sequential decoder's error probability low even with very low signal-to-noise ratios. Furthermore, they prove through both analysis and simulation that using the polar cutoff rate as the bias enhances the average computational speed of the sequential decoder.

We introduce a novel method for robust 6-DoF object tracking and pose estimation in monocular RGB videos, specifically designed for human-object interactions. Leveraging large-scale pretrained vision transformers, this approach effectively addresses monocular challenges such as varying scales, occlusions, and ambiguous depth cues. By modeling interactions as hand-object pairs through shared embedding spaces, we ensure occluded regions contribute contextually to both individual predictions. Additionally, mutual distillation of features between the shared models enhances their separate output quality. Tracking is achieved by maintaining a data-association graph that links detected objects and hands across frames, with a novel loss function refining 6-DoF positions by exploiting temporal consistency in embedded features. Extensive testing on two datasets demonstrates a substantial performance gain over prior state-of-the-art methods.
